newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SOCCER-STEAUA HIT BACK TWICE TO BEAT PSG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STEAUA HIT BACK TWICE TO BEAT PSG.

text.p: Steaua Bucharest twice came from behind to beat Paris St. Germain 3-2 in their European Cup preliminary round first-leg clash on Wednesday.
Veteran Marius Lacatus hit the winner 11 minutes from the finish.
PSG, launching dangerous and fast counter-attacks, seized the lead in the 19th minute through Vincent Guerin.
Steaua equalised from a spot kick by Iosif Rotariu in the 54th minute, only for striker Florian Maurice to restore PSG's advantage 10 minutes later from a cross by midfielder Franck Gava on the left.
Lacatus, captain and deputy trainer, played an influential role for Steaua, setting up midfielder Denis Serban for the second equaliser after 71 minutes, then hitting the decisive goal.
Steaua's coach, Mihai Stoichita, said: "I'm very happy we scored three goals against PSG, one of the most famous European teams, but we have to reinforce our defence for the second leg.
"I don't promise qualification (for the Champions' League) in Paris, but I promise our play there will be even better."
PSG coach Ricardo Gomez said: "I'm sorry to lose at this level of the competition and this was due to our lack of force in attack.
"In Paris, PSG will not allow Steaua's dangerous attackers to get too close to our goal."
